subject: Correct formula for a spatio-temporally varying coefficient regression model?

messages.author: 6205e4b1a72b2445
messages.subject: Correct formula for a spatio-temporally varying coefficient regression model?
parts:
Dear List and Dr. Havard Rue:

I am trying to fit a spatiotemporally varying coefficient regression model. I have a set of panel data that runs for 7 years with 170 spatial units on an irregular lattice. The neighborhood adjacency file (queen contiguity) is created as gb.adj. The original model with the Y as the dependent variable, and X1, X2, X3, X4 (so named in the data table) as covariates plus an intercept.

So the regression model takes the form:

Y = 1 + X1 + X2 + X3 + X4

Instead of running a spatial panel regression analysis or a spatially varying coefficient panel regression model, I read in the Blangiardo and Cameletti's <Spatial and Spatio-temporal Bayesian Models with R-INLA> that I might actually be able to produce regression coefficients that vary both spatially and temporally (as in Chapter 7 of the referred book for the four types of spatio-temporal interactions). I organized my data in such a way so that the region ID ran faster and the temporal ID ran slower as in:

id.region id.time
1            1
2            1
3            1
4            1
5            1
......
1            2
2            2
3            2
4            2
5            2
...

All the region ID and time ID are replicated five times for the intercept and the four covariates.

But then I am lost on how to actually produce an effective formula to obtain the spatiotemporally varying coefficients since my model is "Gaussian" with covariates, the model in the book is "poisson" without covariates. Still, I try to replicate what I learned from the book and communication with Dr. Havard Rue and conjured a formula like this:

fm.stv<- Y ~ f(id.region.int, model = "bym", graph = gb.adj, group = id.time.int, control.group = list(model = "ar1")) +
             f(id.region.X1, X1, model = "bym", graph = gb.adj, group = id.time.X1, control.group = list(model = "ar1")) +
             f(id.region.X2, X2, model = "bym", graph = gb.adj, group = id.time.X2, control.group = list(model = "ar1")) +
             f(id.region.X3, X3, model = "bym", graph = gb.adj, group = id.time.X3, control.group = list(model = "ar1")) +
             f(id.region.X4, X4, model = "bym", graph = gb.adj, group = id.time.X4, control.group = list(model = "ar1"))
                       

mod.stv.intIV <- inla(fm.stv,family="gaussian",data=stv.data,
                  control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE),
                  control.compute=list(dic=TRUE,cpo=TRUE))

The run time varies quite a bit from a few minutes to sometimes hours (especially when using the "besagproper" model). It would produce results, but when I tried to extract the random effects from the model, and followed the code to produce the spatiotemporally varying coefficients for each time period and spatial units, the results seemed to be rather unrealistic.

I suspect that I might not specify the spatio-temporal model correctly (I tried to use "rw2" for the control.group, which runs faster, but the results are not ideal, either). My questions are:

1. Is this the correct way to specify a formula for estimating the spatio-temporally varying coefficient regression model, assuming that the coefficients indeed interact in both space and time (in such scenarios that the changes of one location's covariates will not only have influences on the outcome of that location, but on neighboring locations in both space and time in an autocorrelated manner)?

2. What other models (except for "bym", "besag", "besagproper" for the spatial, and "ar1" or "rw1", "rw2" models for the temporal (control group)) can be used to produce spatio-temporally varying coefficients?

Thank you very much for this excellent package that has so much potential for a lot of social science problems.

Best,
Danlin Yu

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Correct formula for a spatio-temporally varying coefficient regression model?
parts:
to use f() as a varying regression coefficient, then we use

f(idx, x, model=..)

which creates f[idx] * x[idx] as the effect, instead of just f[idx].
that seems correct.

be aware when using models that default have constr=TRUE, like

f(idx, x, model="rw2")

as then the coefficients sum to zero and this is not what you want, so
then add constr=FALSE.


you can order your data in any way you like, its all about

f(idx,x, ..., group=g)

as the i'th data point has contribution from idx[i], x[i] and g[i].

and recall 'g' are integers from 1, 2, ..., n.groups


I would guess that 'bym', 'bym2' models are not what you want, and doing
a kronecker product with the AR1 is a little strange. try model='besag'
and add scale.model=TRUE, and then use the ar1 group model.

'besag.proper' I do not like much...


for the time, the 'ar1' is the default choice for group, and come with
one hyperparameter.


If you're concerned about speed, then use

control.inla=list(strategy="adaptive")

and check out the PARDISO library

inla.pardiso()

assuming you're using Linux or Mac (not avail on Win yet)

H

Dear Dr. Havard:

These are extremely helpful instructions. A few more questions follow:

1. Other than model "rw2" that default to sum the coefficients to zero
(constr = TRUE), will the spatial models such as "besag", "bym", also
default to sum the coefficients to zero as well? Or will it be safe to
just set constr = FALSE for all the models just to make sure that the
coefficients are not sum to zero.

2. I added the control.inla = list(strategy = "adaptive") in INLA's
parameter list, but the calibration is still taking way too long (past
the hour mark). I signed up for the PARDISO library last night with my
school email address, but did not receive the license file, and now I
realized that I am a windows PC user, so that probably will not matter
much since I cannot use it anyways. Any timeline that it will be
available on Windows machines? If not, I'll see if I can use a Linux
shell on the windows to make it work.

Thank you very much for all the pointers.

Best,

Danlin
